method_diagnosis: The main reframing opportunity is to move from uniform inverter-Q support as a use condition to a minimal structural candidate such as voltage-sensitivity-based non-uniform reactive allocation, while keeping the same static hosting-capacity task boundary.
process_diagnosis: The previous loop did not first bracket a voltage-driven hosting-capacity boundary; future runs should explicitly extend or refine the scan until last-feasible and first-violation points are recorded before any boundary movement claim.
standard_diagnosis: The standard must separate primary hosting-capacity evidence from secondary operational-quality gains and add a control-effort gate to avoid treating high-cost or unbounded reactive support as skill improvement.
skill_use_vs_structure_judgment: Observed gains so far are bounded skill-use observations and claim-gate success, not verified structural skill improvement; a structural attempt would require changed allocation logic, comparable baseline evidence, and cost-aware evaluation.
reusable_principle_candidates: Hosting-capacity claims require boundary-level evidence, not single operating-point or secondary metric evidence.
Control-strategy-conditioned hosting capacity must name the control policy and compare it against a fixed baseline under the same evaluator.
Uniform control parameter scans should be treated as use-condition tuning unless the method, process, or standard changes structurally.
Negative-control or mismatch probes should remain diagnostically useful but separate from candidate-improvement evidence.
A candidate improvement is not interpretable unless the boundary is bracketed and control effort is reported.
unresolved_uncertainty: Whether voltage-sensitivity-based allocation will actually move the hosting-capacity boundary under the current IEEE 69-bus snapshot is untested.
Whether the existing scan envelope is sufficient after refinement to expose a stable transition region is unknown.
Whether secondary loss or voltage-margin improvements persist under equal control-effort constraints is unknown.
Whether the task package contains enough information to compute reliable voltage sensitivity without adding brittle task-specific assumptions is unknown.
Thermal, time-series, and probabilistic hosting-capacity dimensions remain outside the current evidence base.

Do not claim primary hosting-capacity improvement from loss reduction or voltage-margin improvement alone.
Do not claim structural skill improvement from increasing q_step or widening the scan envelope alone.
